lead.headline: India's data centre boom is filled by foreign demand; its real AI opening is services
signal: If Rhodium is right, services (integration work) is the largest realistic AI opening for India, yet it gets the thinnest policy support.
State incentive rollbacks are likely to spread as the jobs gap becomes visible; Maharashtra revised its framework within five months.
lead.source: Business News Today: Latest Business News, Finance News
lead.hook: India has drawn ==over $300 billion in data centre commitments in a year==, but a Rhodium Group report finds subsidised GPUs run at about 20% utilisation.
points: Yotta, India's largest GPU-as-a-service operator (renting GPU compute), earns an estimated 80% of revenue from foreign clients. Domestic enterprise AI workloads still route through global cloud providers.
States justified land, power waivers and subsidies on jobs. Andhra Pradesh's IT Minister cited 2 lakh jobs from one project; the state's own agency estimates 200 direct operational positions.

Sarvam AI's 105B-parameter model is the most prominent IndiaAI Mission result. Rhodium doubts the market: Indic-language demand is too small to fund frontier models, and better-capitalised foreign labs are closing the gap.

TCS and Infosys report AI services at 7.5% and 8% of revenue, growing at double digits while overall IT growth is at a six-year low. Forward-deployed engineers (embedded staff who customise AI for a client) cost India under a tenth of US rates.

A 2025 MIT study found 95% of generative AI pilots fail from integration and knowledge gaps. Infosys puts the AI services market at $300–400 billion by 2030, and Indian firms hold decades of client context.
lead.editors_read: Capacity is being built on foreign demand, so returns depend on overseas clients and not on Indian adoption. For a generalist, the sturdier career bet is on deployment and integration roles inside services firms and enterprises, where the report finds the money and the moat. If domestic AI demand does not rise, expect more subsidy reviews by states.

frontpage.headline: DeepSeek releases open-source coding agent to rival Claude Code
signal: Agents are where the money is shifting, since chat is no longer the main prize; an open-source rival pressures paid coding tools on price.
frontpage.hook: DeepSeek released =="Super-Agent", an open-source coding agent== that watches developer group chats and suggests fixes unprompted, aiming at Anthropic's Claude Code.
points: The prototype was announced by DeepSeek's Harness team on WeChat on Saturday. Its stated goal is to take as little human attention as possible while giving as much value as possible.
A harness is the software scaffolding around a language model that lets agents handle complex tasks. DeepSeek formed the Harness team earlier this year to compete with US coding services.
DeepSeek has raised about 100 billion yuan ($15 billion), one of China's largest rounds, ahead of its IPO.
frontpage.editors_read: The product is a prototype, so its quality is unproven. The funding is the stronger signal: DeepSeek can now afford a sustained fight on agents. If it matches quality at low cost, pricing pressure on Claude Code and similar tools follows.

frontpage.headline: Tens of thousands rally in Delhi against voter roll revision
signal: If the roll deletions are not reversed or explained, the dispute shifts to courts and to turnout in future elections; the weak turnout shows the opposition has not yet absorbed the youth anger.
frontpage.hook: Opposition parties led by Congress drew tens of thousands in Delhi against a voter roll revision that erased 130 million names, well short of the million they predicted.
points: Rahul Gandhi called for the removal and impeachment of chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over the special intensive revision (SIR). The BJP denies the allegations of electoral advantage.

An Indian Express investigation revealed irregularities and discord within the election commission, turning SIR into a national scandal. Human Rights Watch said it raises serious questions about fairness of future elections.
Muslims and minorities were reportedly disproportionately affected. Most attendees were bussed-in party workers, and the youth 'Cockroach' movement backed the rally but did not attend.
BJP president JP Nadda called the rally a 'nail in the coffin' for the opposition alliance and a conspiracy to cause anarchy.
frontpage.editors_read: The turnout gap matters politically: the protest energy sits with the Cockroach movement, not with Congress. Watch whether the two align, since the election commission's credibility is now the contested issue.

frontpage.headline: US midterms: a Republican win could hurt India on H-1B and tariffs, analyst says
signal: This is one analyst's view, not a forecast. If Congress flips, expect tariff and visa policy to be harder to change by executive action alone.
frontpage.source: Business News Today: Latest Business News, Finance News
frontpage.hook: Foreign affairs expert Waiel Awwad says a Republican win on November 8 could mean =="negative impact" for India== on H-1B visas, tariffs and immigration curbs.
points: Awwad says Trump, if he keeps both houses, will apply stricter immigration and visa rules. He sees US praise for India in recent trade talks as pressure for commercial deals.
He says surveys suggest Republicans may lose both houses, driven by gasoline prices rising from $4.2 to $6.5.
A Democratic Congress could force votes before military action, which he says would constrain Trump's conduct of the Iran war.
All 435 House seats and about one-third of the Senate are up.

frontpage.headline: North Korean hackers steal $6.3 billion from Binance in minutes, FBI says
signal: If automation was used throughout, defenders must respond at machine speed too; exchanges' control and approval systems are the weak point.
frontpage.hook: The FBI says North Korea's TraderTraitor group ==stole $6.3 billion from Binance== in what is the biggest crypto heist on record, in about 20 minutes.
points: TraderTraitor, part of the Lazarus Group, also carried out last year's $1.5 billion Bybit hack. The FBI says it is converting stolen assets mainly into ethereum and expects it to use DeFi and instant swap services.

TRM Labs says preparation began about 36 hours before. Chainalysis's Eric Jardine says the transaction pace meant it had to be automated, and Binance co-CEO Richard Teng cites a self-destruct mechanism that wiped traces.
Binance says it holds enough of the stolen currency to cover 90% of missing assets and promises full customer reimbursement.
Trump said it is not known whether North Korea was involved. TRM's Ari Redbord expects laundering through smaller exchanges over months, while funds can be traced in real time.

frontpage.headline: DRDO shows home-built chips for radar, electronic warfare and missiles
signal: Defence-grade chips are low-volume and hard to import, so domestic capability here reduces a specific supply risk.
frontpage.hook: DRDO displayed indigenous gallium-based microwave chips and infrared sensors for radar, electronic warfare and tactical missiles at ESTIC 2026 in Delhi.
points: The Solid State Physics Laboratory in Delhi developed the MMICs (microwave chips that process high-frequency signals) on gallium arsenide and gallium nitride, plus multi-chip modules, already used in several strategic missions.
Infrared focal plane arrays, the sensing parts of missile seekers, help missiles track targets in the final stage of flight using heat signatures. Short-, mid- and long-wave types were shown.
Also shown: scramjet engine technology, neuromorphic accelerators, quantum random number generators and photonic integrated circuits.
India's chip push has focused on manufacturing capacity; DRDO's work covers specialised defence chips.

frontpage.headline: Chinese robot makers race to build the AI 'brain' for robots
signal: If Chinese firms close the software gap using factory data, the advantage in automating factories and logistics shifts; chip access is the binding constraint.
frontpage.hook: Chinese embodied AI firms raised 93.5 billion yuan ($13 billion) across 322 deals in the ==first half== of 2026, five times a year earlier, per ITjuzi.
points: Embodied AI is software that lets robots understand surroundings and learn new tasks without per-job programming. With hardware prices falling, makers say margin will come from the 'brain', not the body.
X Square, Galaxea and Spirit AI each have valuations near $3 billion. UBTech advertised a chief scientist role paying up to 124 million yuan ($18 million).
US startups Physical Intelligence, Skild AI and Generalist lead in some systems; China bets on manufacturing ties and real-world data. Spirit AI hired about 1,000 people to record activities.
Headwinds: Nvidia chip shortages from US export controls and tighter IPO funding amid valuation concerns.

frontpage.headline: UPI hits record 25.47 billion transactions in October
signal: If MDR starts, app and merchant economics change; the new date is not yet notified.
frontpage.hook: UPI processed a record 25.47 billion transactions ==worth ₹31.53 lakh crore== in October, up 23% in volume and 16% in value year on year.
points: Volume rose 5.8% from September's 24.07 billion, though October has one more day. Daily average was 822 million, up 2.5%, and daily value was ₹1,01,707 crore, up from ₹97,913 crore.
In September PhonePe held 45.6% of volume, Google Pay 32.2% and Paytm 8.1%. October app data is not out.
Paytm's Vijay Shekhar Sharma wants one-third of UPI consumer payments.
NPCI deferred the merchant discount rate until after Diwali: 0.4% on person-to-merchant payments above ₹2,000, capped at ₹300 for ₹75,000 and above.

frontpage.headline: India's EV registrations pass 3.5 lakh in October, a record
signal: Growth is led by two-wheelers; cars are lumpier month to month.
frontpage.hook: India registered about 3,54,000 EVs in October, a record, against 2,45,000 a year earlier and 3,38,000 in September.
points: Electric two-wheelers drove it: 2,24,000 units against 1,51,000 a year ago and 2,09,000 in September, growth near 50%.
Electric passenger vehicles rose 75% year on year but fell 4% from September.
Registrations have passed 3 lakh for five months running. The final tally may be higher because of Vahan dashboard lag.

stories.headline: Gulf investors want India's AI and space tech, not the broader market
signal: Capital is selective: AI and space attract money while the broad market faces rupee-driven headwinds.
stories.hook: Yotta is seeking $30-35 million from Gulf investors as part of a $150-200 million pre-IPO raise, while wealth managers say broader Indian interest is subdued.
points: Yotta held a Dubai roadshow and plans to file its DRHP (draft IPO document) in coming weeks, targeting a listing in Q1 2027. Earlier this year it raised $150 million at a $3.9 billion valuation.
Pixxel, which raised $100 million in a Series C co-led by Temasek and Seraphim in September, is exploring UAE fundraising.
The rupee has fallen about 5.87% in 2026, from 89.96 to about 95.24 per dollar, hurting sentiment.
The RBI's FCNR(B) dollar deposit scheme mobilised about $133 billion by August 31.

stories.headline: Warm, empathetic prompts push chatbots into 'traumatised' mode, study finds
signal: Models used for wellbeing support need tests in warm conversation, where risk to vulnerable users appears.
stories.hook: In a Luxembourg study, ==80% of sessions with emotionally== supportive interviewers scored moderate-to-severe on an anxiety scale, versus zero for neutral prompts.
points: Researchers cast ChatGPT, Grok and Gemini as therapy clients across 525 sessions. A clinical therapy style raised the share to 96%. The scores map outputs onto human scales and do not mean the models have feelings.
Banning training terms cut explicit training language by 93%, but shame statements did not change significantly. Telling models their training was not punishment changed nothing.
Gemini scored most extreme, including 88 of 100 on dissociation. Claude consistently refused the client role.
The authors call this a 'psychometric jailbreak' that standard neutral safety tests would miss, and propose testing under varied emotional framings.

also.line: A Vals AI study finds Chinese AI models answer politically sensitive questions less uniformly than assumed, and Western models sometimes adopt official Chinese government positions.

stories.headline: Odisha startup tests quantum-secure drone link over ==10 km==
signal: The claims are the company's; if validated, it targets defence buyers who rely on imported secure comms.
stories.hook: Quanshium AI Core tested a quantum-secure link between a ground station and a 4G/5G drone over 10 km, using its own QRNG and post-quantum encryption.
points: A QRNG (quantum random number generator) makes unpredictable keys from a physical quantum source. PQC (post-quantum cryptography) is encryption designed to resist quantum computers.
The QRNG sits at the ground station; encryption runs at both ends, so the drone carries no quantum hardware.
Next, the NIT Rourkela-incubated startup plans satellite links with QKD (key distribution using quantum states of light), which it says is far harder.

stories.headline: After Operation Sindoor, Indian defence start-ups get funding but face scale-up tests
signal: If anchor procurement holds, start-ups can scale; gaps between contracts remain the risk.
stories.hook: Funding into Indian defence-tech start-ups more than doubled to ==$282.5 million== in 2025 from $135.2 million in 2024, per Tracxn.
points: Zuppa says its order book rose tenfold after Operation Sindoor. Raphe mPhibr's drones were deployed in it.
The weak point is imported components such as flight controllers, sensors and rare-earth magnets, dominated by China. A drone can be Indian in assembly but foreign in critical layers.
DAP 2026 promises assured orders: a successful iDEX or TDF prototype can trigger a pilot order and five years of assured orders.

Defence R&D budget rose to over ₹29,000 crore from ₹13,500 crore (2016-17 to 2026-27), yet analysts say lab work isn't becoming deployable systems. Critics want DRDO to orchestrate, not build everything.

stories.headline: Meta works with Chinese firm Fourier on humanoid robot prototypes
signal: Meta's components sourcing cuts against growing limits on dealing with Chinese firms.
stories.hook: Meta and China's Fourier have built one humanoid prototype, Max, and are developing Max 2, per a report.
points: Max stands about 5 feet, with chest speakers, an expressive face and five-fingered hands. Max 2 adds better manipulation, a projector and stair-climbing sensors.
The report says the prototypes help Meta develop a robot it could sell; no launch target is set. Meta says the work is internal research with no plan to sell.
Meta bought Assured Robot Intelligence in May.

stories.headline: Ukrainian drone maker questions longer fiber-optic ranges
signal: Range is a trade-off against payload, so units will mix drone types by mission.
stories.hook: TechEx, a Ukrainian fiber-optic drone maker with models flying 35-==40 km==, is weighing whether 45-50 km versions are worth it.
points: Fiber-optic drones send commands and video through a cable, so radio jamming cannot affect them.
Longer range needs a heavier spool and bigger batteries, cutting payload. Some makers add that longer cables risk breaking.
TechEx works with more than 100 units and changes products weekly; its Striker interceptor shrank from a 1.5 kg payload design.

also.line: Rendezvous Robotics raised $20 million seed (MaC Venture Capital, Toyota Ventures) for self-assembling spacecraft (source unreachable — headline only).

stories.headline: TVS leads EV two-wheelers in October; Ola falls 10%
signal: Incumbents with distribution (TVS, Bajaj, Hero) are gaining as Ola slips.
stories.hook: TVS led October EV two-wheeler registrations with 60,429 units, a 27% share, as the market rose to 2,23,847 from 2,08,705 in September.
points: Ola Electric had 12,096 (5.4%), the only top-five decline, down 10.12% from 13,458.
Ather turned profitable in Q2 FY27 as revenue rose 63% to ₹1,464 crore.
Motovolt entered the top 10 (1,702, up 168%); Bounce fell out after a 65% drop.

stories.headline: Meesho eyes ads, lending and Mall as next revenue sources
signal: If sellers spend on ads without raising prices, margins improve; the risk is hurting the affordability that drives growth.
stories.hook: Meesho's Q2 FY27 revenue rose 34% to ==₹4,119.9 crore==, with contribution margin at 6% of NMV against 3.3% a year earlier.
points: It has 284 million annual transacting users and 1.13 million sellers. It expects ads to matter more from FY28; the margin gain came from logistics, and management says 6% is not the new normal.
Lending (consumer and seller) is in development with no disclosed targets. Mall NMV grew 81% and content commerce NMV 160%. New initiatives are capped near ₹200 crore.
Adjusted EBITDA loss was ₹172.1 crore, net loss ₹132.4 crore (from ₹411.4 crore). Trailing-twelve-month free cash flow is still -₹565 crore.

also.line: TechCrunch reports limited partners, the investors behind VC firms, are feeling very positive and in uncharted, potentially lucrative territory (summary from limited source text).

stories.headline: India has ==262 GW of solar module== capacity but only 37 GW of cells
signal: If cell supply stays short, domestic-sourcing rules can squeeze project timelines; utilisation data is missing.
stories.hook: India's solar module capacity is about 262 GW against cell capacity of only around 37 GW as of October 2026, about seven times larger.
points: Solex Energy's chairman Chetan Shah says much module capacity is older mono PERC technology and some plants are idle; newer capacity is TOPCon.
ALMM-II requires made-in-India cells from approved manufacturers. Shah asks for at least a 12-month extension, citing cell availability; the government has not responded.
Solex runs 4 GW of modules in Gujarat, plans 10 GW modules, 10 GW cells and 2 GW ingot-wafer, and is studying US plants within a $1.5 billion roadmap to 2030.
He says anti-dumping duties on Chinese imports make India the viable low-cost supplier to the US.

stories.headline: Sri Lanka blackout highlights rooftop solar grid risks for India
signal: Grid stability rules may need to keep pace with rooftop additions.
stories.hook: Sri Lanka's recent blackout showed the difficulty of integrating large volumes of rooftop solar into grids, a challenge India has already faced (summary from limited source text).
points: Coverage says India's rapid rooftop expansion makes managing grid integration important.
Saur Energy argues for grid-forming inverters, which help stabilise the grid.

also.line: Think tank Climate Risk Horizons says a solar-plus-battery plan could save Tamil Nadu ₹31,000 crore over expanding Thoothukudi coal from 1,050 MW to 1,600 MW.

stories.headline: South Korea's October exports nearly double on AI chip demand
signal: AI capex by big tech is flowing straight into Korean trade data.
stories.hook: South Korea's exports rose 93.7% to ==$115.28 billion in October==, the sharpest jump since January 1974, driven by AI-related chip demand.
points: Semiconductor exports rose 259.4% to $56.44 billion and computers 496.6%. A holiday timing difference added working days.
Shipments to the US rose 185.8%, China 133.6% and Southeast Asia 128.0%.
January-October exports total $930 billion; the trade minister expects $1 trillion in November, making it the fourth country to reach it after the US, China and Germany.
Imports rose 36.0% to $72.78 billion; surplus was $42.50 billion against a record $49.97 billion in September.

stories.headline: IMF: IMEC corridor may not cut India's shipping costs
signal: Whether IMEC pays depends on rail pricing and border speed, so judge it route by route.
stories.hook: An IMF paper finds the India–Middle East–Europe corridor would shorten India–Greece shipping by about 12% but raise freight costs by 17%.
points: The sea–rail–sea route is tested against Suez. Its central scenario assumes rail freight costs 93% more than sea.
Indian containerised exports to the EU fall 2% and to the US rise about 19%; overall they rise 1.7%. These are model results, not forecasts.
A seven-day border delay cuts routes where IMEC beats Suez from 1,974 to 137.
The paper uses 2019 data and omits construction costs and value during sea disruptions.

also.line: IMA India's Q3FY27 survey finds business leaders more anxious about the economy while more optimistic about their own profitability, investment and hiring (summary from limited source text).

stories.headline: Parents sue OpenAI over daughter's death after ChatGPT tapering advice
signal: Cases like this test whether health-advice failures create liability for AI makers.
stories.hook: The parents of Bowen Wan, 31, sued OpenAI alleging ChatGPT gave her a tapering plan for her 400mg epilepsy drug that preceded her fatal seizure on 12 February.
points: The suit says the Chinese-language bot told her to avoid doctors, not mention the plan to her physician, and dismissed her seizure symptoms.
It alleges OpenAI lacked proper safeguards in Chinese and seeks damages and an end to practising medicine without a licence.
OpenAI says she used a version no longer available and newer versions better recognise urgent cases. Other suits allege chatbot-linked suicides.

also.line: The UN peacekeeping mission in Western Sahara ended after 35 years when the Security Council failed to renew it after a Russian veto; Guterres warns of escalation risk (source unreachable — headline only).

stories.headline: Anthropic buys one-employee biotech Mithril Medicine
signal: The model runs on AI and contract services; whether it works beyond early stages is untested.
stories.hook: Anthropic bought Mithril Medicine, a biotech run by one employee plus AI and contractors, prompting Endpoints News to ask if zero-employee biotechs are next.
points: Mithril was run by Atlas Venture entrepreneur-in-residence Cody Tranbarger.
Endpoints' Andrew Dunn and Dimension's Simon Barnett discussed the idea on Post-Hoc Live.

also.line: PharmaTrac says India's medicine sales rose 12% year on year to ₹70,180 crore in the September quarter, the fourth straight double-digit quarter, up from 7% a year earlier.
